The trigger depends on the caller reciting a card unprompted, since nothing asks for one and payments go through Stripe links. Once that happens, the stores listed (transcript turns, voice_sessions.transcript, knowledge_chunks.content, ai_runs, the LLM provider, Langfuse if content capture is on) all receive the PAN, along with the Twilio and S3 audio. High is reasonable because it pulls those stores into PCI scope, though it is incidental capture rather than systematic.
verification.corrected_fix: Keep the Luhn-validated scrubber (13-19 digits, optional space or dash groups) and apply it at callerTranscriptText, on user-role text in LLMGateway.complete before dispatch and snapshot, and in redactTextForExport and scrubPii, where the residual detector should also flag grouped digits. Add redact=pci to the Deepgram URL. Twilio Gather speechResult cannot be redacted upstream, so the app-side chokepoint is the main control. Drop 'pauseRecording on detection' as the audio control: detection happens after the utterance, so the PAN is already in that recording. Instead flag the recording (e.g. pci_detected) and purge or trim its audio from S3 and from Twilio (see PRIV-2), then speak a deterministic line telling the caller not to read card numbers and that a pay link will be texted. Pausing is only useful as an extra step for anything said after detection.

findings.title: Retention sweep deletes only the S3 copy of each call recording; the Twilio-hosted original is never deleted and recording_url keeps pointing at it
findings.trigger: Every inbound AI call arms `<Start><Record>` (twilio-adapter.ts:751-757). When the recording completes, the webhook fetches the MP3 from Twilio with platform credentials, PUTs it to S3, and inserts voice_recordings with recording_url (recording-webhook.ts:339-363). Voicemail follows the same path (voicemail-status-route.ts:472-478). Past recording_retention_days, RecordingRetentionWorker calls `deps.storage.deleteObject(bucket, key)` (recording-retention-worker.ts:787-788) and stamps purged_at. The Twilio recording resource is never deleted at ingest, at purge, or anywhere else, and recording_url is left on the row.
findings.impact: Call audio (caller voice, everything said, including any PAN from PRIV-3) lives indefinitely at a third party, past the tenant's retention horizon and past legal 'deletion'. The purge audit event (`voice_recording.purged` with hadStoredObject) tells the operator the audio is gone when the primary copy still exists and is fetchable through the retained recording_url with account credentials. That is a false deletion record for SOC 2 / DPA purposes.
findings.evidence: recording-webhook.ts:339-353: `const bytes = await fetchRecording(recordingUrl, deps.twilioAccountSid, deps.twilioAuthToken); ... await uploadObject(uploadUrl, bytes, contentType);`, with no DELETE afterwards. Repo-wide grep for Twilio recording deletion (`Recordings/`, `.recordings`, `method: 'DELETE'`) finds only the pause call `/Calls/{CallSid}/Recordings/Twilio.CURRENT.json` with Status=paused (recording-control.ts:108-112). recording-retention-worker.ts:787-788: `if (row.storageBucket && row.storageKey) { await deps.storage.deleteObject(row.storageBucket, row.storageKey); }`. markPurged (209-218) only sets purged_at. purgeDerived (221-255) nulls transcript but not recording_url.
findings.fix: S3 is the system of record, so delete the Twilio copy right after a successful S3 upload and DB insert in recording-webhook.ts and voicemail-status-route.ts: `DELETE /2010-04-01/Accounts/{AccountSid}/Recordings/{RecordingSid}.json` behind an injectable `TwilioRecordingDeleter` seam shaped like RecordingControl (timedFetch, auth token never logged, 404 treated as done, failure logged and retried by a sweep). For legacy rows, add the same delete to the retention worker's per-row purge, derived from the RecordingSid embedded in recording_url, and null voice_recordings.recording_url in markPurged. Record `twilioDeleted` in the purge audit metadata.
findings.test: Unit tests with mocked fetch: the webhook issues the DELETE only after the S3 PUT and the insert succeed, never when the upload fails, and treats 404 as success; the retention worker issues the Twilio delete for a legacy row and records it in the audit event. Docker-gated integration test pinning that markPurged nulls recording_url (real column) and that a re-run is idempotent.

verification.reasoning: recording-webhook.ts:339-353 and voicemail-status-route.ts:460-472 fetch the MP3 from Twilio, PUT it to S3 and insert voice_recordings with recording_url. Neither deletes the Twilio resource. A repo grep finds only one Twilio Recordings call, the pause in recording-control.ts:111. The retention sweep calls storage.deleteObject on the S3 key only (recording-retention-worker.ts:787-788). markPurged only sets purged_at, and the voice_recording.purged audit event records hadStoredObject. The Twilio original therefore outlives the tenant's retention horizon and the purge record. Nothing in the code configures Twilio-side external storage or auto-delete either; the docs do not mention one. Tenant deprovision closes the Twilio subaccount, which Twilio purges after about 30 days, so the gap is limited to per-recording retention and per-subject deletion. Those are exactly the paths that matter. Nothing reads recording_url after insert, so deleting the Twilio copy right after the S3 upload breaks no downstream consumer.
verification.corrected_fix: Make two changes to the proposed fix. (1) Do not null voice_recordings.recording_url in markPurged. It is the per-recording idempotency key in recordInboundCall (voice-service.ts:539-545), and once the Twilio resource is gone it is a dead pointer that holds no PII. (2) Build the DELETE URL from the recording URL itself (/2010-04-01/Accounts/{AC}/Recordings/{RE}.json), not from the platform AccountSid. Calls run on per-tenant subaccounts (integrations/twilio/provisioning.ts), so the recording lives under the subaccount; master credentials can delete it on that path. The rest stands: delete after the S3 PUT and DB insert succeed, treat 404 as done, retry from the sweep for legacy or failed rows, and record twilioDeleted in the purge audit metadata.

findings.title: No data-subject erasure path: customer removal is archive-only, and AI artifacts tied to a caller cannot be deleted short of purging the whole tenant
findings.trigger: A homeowner who called a tenant's AI line sends the tenant (the controller) a CCPA/GDPR deletion request. The only per-customer control is POST /api/customers/:id/archive (routes/customers.ts:325), and archiveCustomer only sets is_archived/archived_at (customer.ts:551-555). Everything else stays: the caller's call_transcript_turns, voice_sessions.transcript, voice_recordings and audio, call_summaries, knowledge_chunks (raw `content` beside `content_scrubbed`, schema.ts:1661-1662; retrievable into future prompts), and every ai_runs row carrying their words. The only hard delete is platform-admin tenant deprovision (admin-tenants.ts:43), which wipes the entire tenant.
findings.impact: Neither the tenant nor the platform can satisfy a deletion request within statutory windows (CCPA: 45 days). AI artifacts persist for at least 365 days, and ai_runs forever, because it has no customer or session key (schema.ts:175-192). For an enterprise customer this blocks the DPA: the processor cannot honor the controller's erasure instruction. The spec states the requirement directly: 'Deletion on request must reach all four, not just the audio file' (RIVET_COMMS_SPEC.md:90). Only the SLA (D17) is open, not the capability.
findings.evidence: customer.ts:551-555: `repository.update(tenantId, id, { isArchived: true, archivedAt: new Date(), updatedAt: new Date() })`. A repo-wide grep for `DELETE FROM (customers|call_transcript_turns|voice_sessions|messages|conversations|knowledge_chunks|ai_runs|voice_recordings)` finds hits only in recording-retention-worker.ts (age-based), and the deprovision path deletes by tenant_id only (deprovision.ts:230-242). No dsar/erasure/forget/anonymize route exists (grep).
findings.fix: Add an owner-only, audited `POST /api/customers/:id/erase` (an explicit human mutation, not an AI proposal) that runs one command-runner executeAudited transaction. Keyed on the customer id plus their phones and the call_sids of their voice_sessions, it deletes call_transcript_turns, call_summaries and knowledge_chunks by source id, nulls voice_sessions.transcript and voice_recordings.transcript, deletes the stored audio (and the Twilio copy, PRIV-2), deletes entity aliases and correction lessons that reference the customer, and scrubs ai_runs. For ai_runs, a migration adds a nullable session_id/customer_id populated from request.metadata.sessionId so rows are findable. Keep consent_events and DNC rows as the suppression record. Hash the phone if counsel requires it.
findings.test: Docker-gated integration test in packages/api/test/integration/: seed two customers in tenant A (each with a session, turns, a recording row, a summary, knowledge chunks and ai_runs rows) and one in tenant B. Erase A's first customer. Assert every listed table holds no rows or text for that customer, the other customer and tenant B are untouched, consent_events survives, and one audit event exists in the same transaction (a forced audit failure rolls the erase back).

verification.reasoning: Confirmed. The only per-customer removal is archiveCustomer, which sets is_archived and archived_at (customer.ts:551-555). The customers router has no DELETE /:id; the only DELETE is for tags. A repo grep for dsar, erasure, erase, forget, anonymize, gdpr and ccpa finds no data-subject path, only the Presidio adapter. The only hard DELETEs on the voice and AI tables are the age-based ones in recording-retention-worker.ts, and the only full purge is platform-admin tenant deprovision, which deletes by tenant_id. The spec's 'Deletion on request must reach all four' (RIVET_COMMS_SPEC.md:90) is not implemented, and D17 is open. Two overstatements bring severity down from high. First, 'neither the tenant nor the platform can satisfy' is too strong: platform ops can still erase by hand with tenant-scoped SQL, and ai_runs rows can be found, expensively, by text search on the caller's phone or name in the JSONB. Second, many DPAs accept a documented manual DSAR process. It is a real product-capability gap that enterprise DPA reviews will raise, but not an exploitable defect.
verification.corrected_fix: An owner-only, audited erase command is the right shape, but the proposed scope leaves out the most obvious PII. It must also scrub the customers row itself: archive leaves name, phone, email and address in place. It must also cover customer_contacts, SMS conversations and message bodies, and customer-linked notes. Financial records (invoices, payments, estimates) are under legal or tax retention: anonymize the customer link and keep the amounts rather than deleting them. Keep consent_events and DNC rows as suppression records, hashing the phone if counsel requires it. For ai_runs, do not depend on a new customer_id column alone, since historical rows will not have it. Combine the new key going forward with a bounded scrub of historical rows that match the subject's voice_session correlation ids, or simply rely on the PRIV-1 age-based purge plus a documented manual step. Ship one Docker-gated integration test that covers both tenant isolation and audit-in-transaction.

findings.title: The AI-identity disclosure skill is built and unit-tested but never wired; production calls replace the FSM's 'I'm a virtual assistant' line with a greeting that has no AI disclosure
findings.trigger: Any inbound PSTN call to an AI line, including callers from California, where the skill's own header says disclosure is required. The FSM emits `ttsPlay('greeting', { template: 'greeting_with_disclosure' })` (transitions.ts:862), which would render "Hi, I'm a virtual assistant" (tts-copy.ts:254). On both transports, bootstrapCallEstablishment substitutes buildTelephonyGreeting(...) for the placeholder (twilio-adapter.ts:1344), and the media-streams adapter then strips the template hint (mediastream-adapter.ts:2779-2783). The caller hears 'Thank you for calling {business}. This is {agentName}.' plus the recording notice. With a tenant-set voiceAgentName (voice-persona-resolver.ts:91), the AI introduces itself under a human name. resolveAiDisclosure / buildAiDisclosureText have zero production importers (grep).
findings.impact: Callers are never told they are talking to an AI, and with a persona name the bot affirmatively presents as a named person. That is the scenario bot- and AI-disclosure laws target; the skill names California's B.O.T. Act, Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §17940. An enterprise legal review will block on a disclosure control the codebase built and silently never ran. Per CLAUDE.md this is the 'built but never wired' class.
findings.evidence: disclose-ai-identity.ts:4-11: "This discloses that the caller is speaking with an AI. Bot-disclosure laws in some states require it (e.g. California's B.O.T. Act, SB 1001). Played at call start, after the greeting ... the greeting-path wiring + consent-ledger/audit are the integration layer." `grep -rn 'resolveAiDisclosure|buildAiDisclosureText|requiresAiDisclosure' src` (excluding the module and tests) returns nothing. twilio-adapter.ts:1270 calls only `discloseRecording({...})`, and nothing passes callerState. en.ts:61-62: `'greeting.opener_default': 'Thank you for calling {{business}}.'`, `'greeting.opener_named': 'Thank you for calling {{business}}. This is {{agent}}.'`.
findings.fix: In bootstrapCallEstablishment (twilio-adapter.ts:1269), resolve the caller's state with the existing `placePhone(from).state` (compliance/us-geography.ts:239), call resolveAiDisclosure({ channel: 'telephony', callerState, businessName, language, customText, tenantEnabled }), and pass the text into buildTelephonyGreeting so it lands after the opener in both the default and persona.greeting branches. Fail safe the same way the recording notice does: an unplaced number discloses. Write an audit or consent-ledger row the same way discloseRecording does. Have counsel confirm the state list; the module itself is flagged 'legal review required'.
findings.test: Unit test that buildTelephonyGreeting includes the AI sentence in the default, named-agent and custom-greeting branches. Handler-level tests on TwilioGatherAdapter.handleInbound and the media-streams establishment with a CA (e.g. 415) and an unplaceable caller ID: assert the first <Say> in the TwiML, or the first synthesized TTS turn, contains the AI disclosure and precedes <Start><Record>.

verification.reasoning: disclose-ai-identity.ts exports requiresAiDisclosure, buildAiDisclosureText and resolveAiDisclosure. A grep of src outside the module finds no importers. bootstrapCallEstablishment calls only discloseRecording (twilio-adapter.ts:1270) and replaces the FSM greeting placeholder with buildTelephonyGreeting (twilio-adapter.ts:1344). Both transports go through it (twilio-adapter.ts:1571 for streams). That greeting is assembled from 'Thank you for calling {business}.' or '... This is {agent}.' plus the recording notice ('This call may be recorded for quality and training purposes...'), and neither says AI. The media-streams adapter strips the template hint once the text is substituted (mediastream-adapter.ts:2779-2783), so the FSM's 'Hi, I'm a virtual assistant' (tts-copy.ts:254) is never spoken. Nothing in the voice prompts or copy discloses AI identity later either; my grep found none. voiceAgentName from tenant_settings becomes the spoken agent name (voice-persona-resolver.ts:91). The legal impact is somewhat overstated. California's B.O.T. Act (SB 1001) targets bots on online platforms used to mislead for a sale or a vote, and whether it covers inbound PSTN calls is unclear. But a disclosure control that was built and silently never run, plus a human persona name, is a real compliance and trust gap. Medium is right.
verification.corrected_fix: Do not gate on placePhone(from).state. Area code is a weak proxy for where the caller is (ported mobiles, VoIP), and the module returns false for an unknown state, which contradicts the 'unplaced number discloses' fail-safe the auditor wants. The simpler and safer fix: on telephony, always pass the disclosure sentence (resolveAiDisclosure with tenantEnabled defaulting to true, or call buildAiDisclosureText directly) into buildTelephonyGreeting in all three branches, including a custom tenant greeting. Keep the per-tenant wording override, and have counsel confirm whether any jurisdiction needs a specific placement. Ledger or audit it the same way discloseRecording does. Tests as proposed: a buildTelephonyGreeting unit test per branch, plus handler-level tests asserting the first <Say> or TTS turn contains the AI sentence.

findings.title: Langfuse content export sends every tenant's prompts and transcripts to a third party behind one global flag, with a regex 'redaction' that lets names, addresses and PANs through and no deprovision purge
findings.trigger: An operator sets LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY/SECRET_KEY and LANGFUSE_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true, for example to debug voice latency. That is one env flag for the whole platform (config.ts:55-58), with the default base URL https://cloud.langfuse.com (config.ts:54). From then on, every gateway completion for every tenant (classify_intent per caller turn, summaries, SMS drafting) exports `redactContentForExport(event.input)` and the reply (trace-exporter.ts:227-228), tagged `tenant:<id>` (182).
findings.impact: Caller transcripts and CRM context leave the boundary to a subprocessor with no tenant-level opt-in or DPA gate. The 'redaction' is heuristic: names are caught only after a salutation or when the first name is in a 58-name list (pii-redact.ts:107), addresses only as Capitalized-Word + street suffix (296), and PANs, spoken digits and gate/alarm codes not at all. Presidio, the repo's real PII backend, is wired only into training-asset ingestion (app.ts:1441). Tenant deprovision purges Postgres, Twilio and S3, but traces stay at Langfuse indefinitely.
findings.evidence: I ran redactTextForExport through a throwaway probe (scratchpad/probe/redact-probe.ts) on realistic voice text: 'Customer: Maria Gonzalez, phone +1 (602) 555-0199, 4821 Bridgewater Road' -> 'Customer: Maria Gonzalez, phone [phone], [address], Phoenix AZ'; 'caller: yeah my name is maria gonzalez and i live at forty eight twenty one bridgewater road' -> unchanged; 'caller: my card is 4111 1111 1111 1111 ... cvv 123' -> unchanged; 'caller: the gate code is 4821 and the alarm code is 9930' -> unchanged; 'Known customer: Priya Raman ([email]), 77 elm st apt 4' (name and address kept). config.ts:51 says 'No prod hard-requirement.' deprovision.ts contains no reference to Langfuse or trace deletion.
findings.fix: (1) In configSchema (the T4-F06 superRefine pattern), refuse LANGFUSE_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true in production/staging unless PRESIDIO_ANALYZER_URL and PRESIDIO_ANONYMIZER_URL are set. Route exported text through the Presidio anonymizer before the regex pass and fail closed: on PresidioUnavailableError, export metadata only. (2) Add the PAN scrubber from PRIV-3 to redactTextForExport. (3) Gate content per tenant with a tenant_settings opt-in read by the exporter, so content ships only for tenants whose DPA covers the subprocessor. (4) Add a best-effort Langfuse trace delete by `tenant:<id>` tag in deprovisionTenant, beside the S3 object cleanup, or require a self-hosted LANGFUSE_BASE_URL with a retention policy.
findings.test: Unit tests in test/ai/gateway/trace-exporter.test.ts with the probe samples above (lowercase spoken name and address, grouped PAN, codes), asserting none survive when a fake Presidio is injected, and that content is dropped (metadata kept) when the fake throws PresidioUnavailableError. Config unit test: NODE_ENV=production with capture=true and no PRESIDIO_* fails validation. Unit test that a tenant without the opt-in gets no input/output on the generation body. Deprovision unit test asserting the trace-delete seam is called with the tenant tag.

verification.reasoning: The code facts check out. LANGFUSE_CAPTURE_CONTENT is a single platform-wide flag (config.ts:55-58) with the base URL defaulting to cloud.langfuse.com. When it is on, buildGenerationBody exports redactContentForExport(input) and redactTextForExport(output), tagged tenant:<id>. Deprovision has no Langfuse cleanup. My own probe matched the auditor's: lowercase spoken names and addresses and spaced PANs pass through unchanged. But the trigger is an operator deliberately opting in, and both defaults are off. Export is a no-op unless both LANGFUSE keys are set, and capture defaults to 'false'. .env.production.example ships the keys empty and capture commented out as false. docs/prod-env-checklist.md says content is 'off by default — voice traces carry caller transcripts'. With capture off, only metadata (tenant id, task type, model, cost, latency) reaches Langfuse, so the deprovision gap matters only when capture is on. This is a hardening gap behind an off-by-default, documented flag, not a live leak. Low severity.
verification.corrected_fix: The fix is oversized. One config guard is enough: in configSchema's superRefine, reject LANGFUSE_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true when NODE_ENV is production or staging unless LANGFUSE_BASE_URL is a self-hosted (non-cloud.langfuse.com) host, or unless an explicit acknowledgement variable is set, and add a config unit test. Adding the PAN scrubber from PRIV-3 to redactTextForExport comes for free with that change. A per-tenant tenant_settings opt-in, a Presidio fail-closed export path and a Langfuse delete-by-tag in deprovision are optional extras, worth doing only if content capture is actually going to be enabled in production.

findings.title: TTS stream failure has no working recovery in production: the buffered fallback always returns mp3 and is discarded, and a failed greeting/disclosure hangs up instead of degrading to Gather
findings.trigger: An ElevenLabs streaming WebSocket blip or stall. A stall is cut at ELEVENLABS_STREAM_INACTIVITY_MS = 4_000 (elevenlabs-stream.ts:20). Path: runTurnWithFiller → ttsProvider.synthesizeStream throws (mediastream-adapter.ts:3200) → recoverTurnAfterStreamFailure → synthesizeBounded → ElevenLabsTtsProvider.synthesize (tts-provider.ts:166). That method always sends `Accept: 'audio/mpeg'` and returns `contentType: 'audio/mpeg'`, so the guard at mediastream-adapter.ts:3358-3381 drops the result and at most a filler clip plays. On the greeting turn, handleStart sees disclosureTurnComplete !== true (1533) and calls failDisclosureClosed. That method only does `this.closeWs(1011, 'disclosure_init_failed')` (1665). Nothing follows `</Connect>` in buildStreamTwiML (twilio-adapter.ts:1603-1612), so Twilio hangs up. Production must use ElevenLabs, because assertTtsProviderSupportsMediaStreams requires synthesizeStream.
findings.impact: During a TTS vendor incident, every new realtime call hears a filler ("one moment"), up to ~6 s of dead air spent on a REST synth that is thrown away, and then a disconnect. The realtime circuit trips only after 2 failures per process and half-opens every 60 s (realtime-health-circuit.ts), so drops recur. Calls already in progress go mute: every reply becomes filler-only, the caller never hears the answers, and mid-call TTS failures never vote the circuit. The hang-up happens even though /voice/gather-fallback is built to speak the disclosure on an undisclosed degrade and voices it with Twilio <Say>, which does not depend on ElevenLabs.
findings.evidence: tts-provider.ts:179 `Accept: 'audio/mpeg'` / :200 `contentType: 'audio/mpeg'`, while the same class's probe already uses `?output_format=pcm_16000` (:218). filler-audio-cache.ts:20: "(`synthesize()` returns mp3, which the media path cannot play)". mediastream-adapter.ts:3376-3379: `'mediastream: buffered TTS fallback returned non-PCM audio, cannot stream — trying filler'`. The Deepgram-open failure degrades: `if (!(await this.attemptDegradeToGather('deepgram_open_failed'))) { this.closeWs(1011, ...) }` (1501-1503). failDisclosureClosed never attempts a degrade (1659-1665). twilio-adapter.ts:1360 latches `session.recordingDisclosed = true` before playback, so a naive degrade would also skip the disclosure in buildDegradeFallbackTwiml (routes/telephony.ts:1241). The VOX-35b unit tests mock the buffered synth as `contentType: 'audio/pcm'` (test/telephony/media-streams/mediastream-adapter.test.ts:1369, 2785), which production never returns.
findings.fix: (1) Add an optional `outputFormat?: 'pcm_16000'` to TtsSynthesizeInput. When it is set, ElevenLabsTtsProvider.synthesize posts to `…/text-to-speech/${voiceId}?output_format=pcm_16000` (the probe's URL) and returns `contentType: 'audio/pcm'`. synthesizeBounded in mediastream-adapter.ts passes it. (2) In failDisclosureClosed, set `session.recordingDisclosed = false` and try `attemptDegradeToGather('disclosure_init_failed')` before `closeWs(1011)`. captureEnabled stays false, so nothing is captured on the stream leg, and gather-fallback speaks `disclose.two_party` in a standalone <Say> before <Gather>. (3) Optionally vote the realtime circuit on repeated mid-call `tts_stream_recovered` failures.
findings.test: Unit (tts-provider): with a mocked fetch, synthesize({outputFormat:'pcm_16000'}) requests `output_format=pcm_16000` and returns 'audio/pcm'. Handler-level (mediastream-adapter.test.ts): use a TTS whose synthesizeStream throws and whose synthesize returns mp3 unless PCM is requested. Assert the greeting PCM streams and capture opens. Second case, TTS fully dead: assert restRedirect is called, closeReason is 'degraded_to_gather' and session.recordingDisclosed === false. Route unit test: gather-fallback for that session emits the disclosure <Say> before <Gather>.

verification.reasoning: I checked each step in the code and it holds. ElevenLabsTtsProvider.synthesize (tts-provider.ts:172-202) always sends Accept: audio/mpeg and returns contentType 'audio/mpeg'. The same class's probe already uses ?output_format=pcm_16000 (:218). recoverTurnAfterStreamFailure (mediastream-adapter.ts:3338-3381) drops any non-PCM result through isRawPcmContentType, and the comment above it says ElevenLabs REST returns mp3. So in production the buffered recovery can never play, and at most a filler clip plays (2 attempts x DEFAULT_TTS_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS of 3s, after the 4s ELEVENLABS_STREAM_INACTIVITY_MS stall). The boot guard (app.ts:4596) forces a synthesizeStream provider, so production is ElevenLabs. On the greeting turn, disclosureTurnComplete is copied from turnRealAudioComplete (2815-2816), and the filler path never sets that flag, so handleStart calls failDisclosureClosed (1543). That method only records a circuit failure, writes an audit and runs closeWs(1011) (1659-1665). It never tries attemptDegradeToGather, unlike the Deepgram-open failure branch (1501-1503). buildStreamTwiML has nothing after </Connect>, so Twilio ends the call. bootstrapCallEstablishment sets session.recordingDisclosed = true (twilio-adapter.ts:1360) before playback, so a naive degrade would skip the disclosure in buildDegradeFallbackTwiml (telephony.ts:1241). The mid-call path only records the 'tts_stream_recovered' voice error and never votes the circuit. restRedirect and fillerCache are both wired in production (app.ts:4836, 4875-4876). ElevenLabsTtsProvider.synthesize then calls ...?output_format=pcm_16000, omits the Accept header and returns 'audio/pcm'. synthesizeBounded in the media-streams adapter always passes it. Leave the default mp3 behavior alone for other synthesize() callers (readback, filler synthesis). (2) In failDisclosureClosed: set session.recordingDisclosed = false (captureEnabled is still false), then `if (await this.attemptDegradeToGather('disclosure_init_failed')) return;`, and only then closeWs(1011). Keep the circuit vote and audit. (3) Do more than vote the circuit for mid-call failures: after a turn whose stream and PCM-REST recovery both failed (or after 2 consecutive tts_stream_recovered turns), vote failure and call attemptDegradeToGather('tts_unavailable'), so the call continues on Twilio <Say> instead of staying filler-only. A PCM REST fallback cannot help when the vendor itself is down.

findings.title: The silence / low-STT / repeated-failure ladder tells the caller "Let me connect you with a team member" and then hangs up: no notify_oncall, no Dial, no voicemail
findings.trigger: A caller is silent for 8 s twice after an agent turn, for example while finding an account number. findings.title: Deepgram `is_final` segments are dispatched as whole caller turns; `speech_final` / UtteranceEnd are ignored, so long utterances split into several LLM turns
findings.trigger: A caller speaks one long sentence with no pause, for example describing the problem and the address. Deepgram (opened with `interim_results=true…&endpointing=600`) finalizes the segment with `is_final:true, speech_final:false` mid-utterance and sends `speech_final:true` only at the endpoint. DeepgramStreamingProvider maps every `is_final` to `type: 'final'` (transcription-providers.ts:599). onTranscriptEvent then treats each final as a complete turn: low-STT gate, filler, hold line, then `withSessionLock(... this.deps.speechTurn(...))` (mediastream-adapter.ts:1976-1983) → twilioAdapter.processCallerUtterance → processor.speechTurn → classifyIntent.
findings.impact: One utterance becomes two or more FSM turns. The first half is classified on its own: the FSM advances, a readback or reprompt starts while the caller is still talking and is barged in, and then the second half is handled as an answer to a prompt the caller never heard. Each fragment costs a full classify (~9k input tokens, up to the 12 s deadline), which uses up the 72k-token session cap and brings cost_cap_exceeded escalations sooner. It also feeds the repeated-intent and low-confidence counters, and the one-shot language detection runs on a fragment. The production phone transport is affected (realtime is default ON).
findings.evidence: transcription-providers.ts:593-602: the parsed type is `{ type?; channel?; is_final?: boolean }`, with no speech_final, and `onEvent({ type: data.is_final ? 'final' : 'partial', … isFinal: data.is_final ?? false })`. No `utterance_end_ms` is requested (:484). The repo's own web client accumulates finals until the endpoint: packages/web/src/hooks/useDeepgramDictation.ts:287-296 `if (d.is_final) { finalsRef.current.push(transcript); … if (continuousRef.current && d.speech_final) { flushUtterance(); …` with the comment "UtteranceEnd is the fallback for finals that arrive without it". It has a test 'flushes accumulated finals on a Deepgram UtteranceEnd event (finals without speech_final)'. No `speech_final` handling exists anywhere in packages/api.
findings.fix: In DeepgramStreamingProvider.openSession, buffer `is_final` transcripts and emit ONE `final` event (joined text, minimum confidence) on `speech_final: true`, or on a Deepgram `UtteranceEnd` message (add `&utterance_end_ms=1000` to buildWsUrl). Forward the buffered `is_final` text as `partial` events in the meantime, so barge-in and the RV-140 interim emergency scan still see it. Flush any buffer in finish(). This mirrors useDeepgramDictation.
findings.test: Unit (test/voice/transcription-providers): drive a fake WebSocket with [is_final:true, speech_final:false 'my furnace stopped'] then [is_final:true, speech_final:true 'at 42 Elm Street'] → exactly one 'final' event with the concatenated transcript. Separate case: UtteranceEnd flushes a final-only buffer. Handler-level (mediastream-adapter.test.ts): the same frame sequence results in speechTurn called once.

verification.reasoning: DeepgramStreamingProvider.openSession (transcription-providers.ts:588-603) parses only {type, channel, is_final}. It emits type 'final' for every is_final:true Results frame and ignores speech_final. The URL (480-484) sets interim_results=true and endpointing=600 but no utterance_end_ms. grep finds no speech_final or UtteranceEnd handling anywhere in packages/api or packages/shared. app.ts:4601/4831 passes the raw provider straight to the adapter, with no aggregating wrapper. onTranscriptEvent (1873-1983) treats each isFinal event as a full turn: low-STT gate, filler, hold line, then withSessionLock(speechTurn). Deepgram documents that with interim_results it finalizes segments (is_final:true, speech_final:false) during long continuous speech, and recommends concatenating is_final segments until speech_final or UtteranceEnd. The repo's web client (useDeepgramDictation.ts) already does this. A long caller description is therefore split across several FSM/LLM turns on the default realtime transport. The fragments queue behind the session lock, and the first fragment's reply is barged in by the caller's continuing interims.
verification.corrected_fix: The auditor's fix is right. Buffer is_final segments inside the provider and emit one 'final' (joined text, minimum confidence) on speech_final:true, or on an UtteranceEnd message (add &utterance_end_ms=1000; this requires interim_results=true, which is already set). Meanwhile forward each buffered segment as a 'partial' so barge-in, latchLifeSafety and the RV-140 interim emergency scan still see it. On finish(), discard the buffer or flush it before close, so a final is never dispatched after the leg has torn down. Add the unit tests and the handler-level test as proposed.

findings.title: Telephony webhook failures end the call: /voice, /gather and /dial-result return 503 "so Twilio retries", but Twilio does not retry 5xx and no VoiceFallbackUrl is provisioned; the catch-all paths hang up instead of taking voicemail
findings.trigger: A Postgres blip or pool exhaustion: pool max 20 with connectionTimeoutMillis 5000 (db/pool.ts:54-56). phoneNumberRepo.findByNumber throws, and resolveInboundTenantId rethrows in prod (telephony.ts:1481-1483). /voice answers `res.status(503)` (469). /gather re-resolves the tenant by DB on EVERY turn, even though the live session already knows it (739-756), so a mid-call blip also 503s. Any throw inside handleGather speaks "We're experiencing technical difficulties. Please try again later." + <Hangup/> (792-797). Separately, Gather turns run with no in-app turn budget: the classify deadline alone is 12 s in prod, against Twilio's ~15 s webhook timeout.
findings.impact: Twilio's default webhook policy retries only connection timeouts, not 5xx responses. No VoiceFallbackUrl is set on any purchased number, so a 5xx or timeout on /voice plays Twilio's generic "an application error has occurred" and drops the call. Action-URL (/gather, /dial-result) failures drop the call mid-conversation. A brief DB brownout therefore drops every inbound call and every live Gather call, with no voicemail, no lead and no callback, even though a DB-free voicemail TwiML exists (the after-hours branch passes callerPhone/dialedNumber on the callback URL for exactly this no-session case).
findings.evidence: telephony.ts:460-469: "Respond 5xx so Twilio retries the webhook; do NOT 200-decline" → `res.status(503).type('text/plain').send('Service temporarily unavailable')`. /gather (746-755): "Respond 503 so Twilio retries the webhook rather than the caller losing their turn." provisioning.ts:200-204 purchases with only `PhoneNumber, VoiceUrl, StatusCallback`. A repo-wide grep for VoiceFallbackUrl / voiceFallbackUrl returns nothing.
findings.fix: (1) Return 200 with `buildVoicemailTwiml({ shopName, recordingStatusCallback: …/voicemail-status, callerPhone: From, dialedNumber: To })`, the shape already used at telephony.ts:539-552, instead of 503 on /voice tenant-lookup failure, and instead of the 'try again later' <Hangup/> in the /voice and /gather catches. (2) On /gather and /dial-result, take the tenant from the in-memory session (`store.get(sid)?.tenantId`, still enforcing sessionBelongsToAnotherTenant) and fall back to the DB lookup only when there is no session. (3) Provision VoiceFallbackUrl (method POST) at purchase, and backfill existing numbers, pointing at a DB-free, signature-verified `/api/telephony/voice/fallback` that returns the same voicemail TwiML.
findings.test: Route-level unit tests (supertest, mocked repos). phoneNumberRepo.findByNumber rejects → /voice returns 200 with `<Record`. /gather with the repo rejecting but a live session in the store → the turn proceeds (handleGather called). handleGather throwing → voicemail TwiML, not <Hangup/>. Provisioning unit test asserts VoiceFallbackUrl is in the purchase params.

verification.reasoning: The outcome is real, but the cited mechanism is not the first failure point, and the fixes as proposed would not take effect. Confirmed: /voice, /gather and /dial-result answer 503 on a tenant-lookup throw (telephony.ts:460-469, 746-755, 786-797 region). The /voice and /gather catch-alls send 'technical difficulties' + <Hangup/>. provisioning.ts:196-205 purchases with only PhoneNumber/VoiceUrl/StatusCallback, and no VoiceFallbackUrl or connection-override retry policy exists anywhere. By Twilio's default policy, 5xx responses are not retried, so a 5xx drops the call with the generic application-error message. The gap in the trigger: every one of these routes sits behind requireTwilioSignature. Its credential resolver (twilio-webhook-credential.ts, createTwilioWebhookCredentialResolver) first runs findByPhoneNumber against tenant_integrations on the same DB. On any DB error it returns outcome 'misconfigured', and the middleware answers 500 (twilio-signature.ts:299-305) before the route runs. In a DB brownout the 500 comes from the middleware in most cases, and the route-level 503 is reached only when the first checkout happens to succeed. Fixes (1) and (2) change code that a DB outage mostly never reaches. Fix (2) also cannot work alone, because even with a known session the resolver's findByTenant path still queries the DB. And a 'DB-free, signature-verified' fallback endpoint is not possible as described: subaccount tenants' tokens live encrypted in that same DB. The side claim of a 12s classify deadline against Twilio's 15s webhook timeout could not be verified.
verification.corrected_fix: (1) The primary fix is to provision VoiceFallbackUrl (POST) at purchase and backfill existing numbers. Point it at a target that needs neither the API's DB nor its signature resolver: either a Twilio-hosted TwiML Bin/Function, or a static API route serving fixed voicemail TwiML (<Say> + <Record recordingStatusCallback=.../api/telephony/recording?callerPhone&dialedNumber>). Rely on the existing /recording To/From fallback, and let its handler 5xx and be retried later, so ingestion happens once the DB is back. (2) Make the signature layer survive short brownouts: keep an in-memory LRU/TTL cache of verified tenant credentials keyed by DID and subaccount, and use it when the DB lookup throws. Without it, no route-level change runs during an outage. (3) Then, as proposed, replace the 503 and the 'try again later' <Hangup/> catch-alls on /voice and /gather with 200 + buildVoicemailTwiml({callerPhone: From, dialedNumber: To}). On /gather and /dial-result, take the tenant from the in-memory session (keeping sessionBelongsToAnotherTenant) and pass it as tenantId to the credential resolver, which then uses the cache. (4) Correct the misleading 'so Twilio retries' comments.

findings.title: Voice session state is process-local: every voice deploy hangs up calls still live after the 25 s drain, and the documented scale-out (NUM_REPLICAS>1 + REDIS_URL) sends /gather turns and stream upgrades to replicas without the session

A Gather call's next /gather reaches the new process, where `store.get` misses (twilio-adapter.ts:2279-2289) → "I'm sorry, your session has ended. Please call again." + hang-up. findings.impact: Contractual uptime cannot be met. Every release that touches the voice process drops in-flight calls; the code knows this and only alarms ('emitDrainAbandonment … teardown below hangs up on real callers'). findings.title: Per-tenant realtime connection cap (50) hangs up the 51st concurrent caller silently instead of routing to Gather
findings.trigger: A tenant has 50 concurrent realtime calls, for example a multi-location enterprise tenant during a heat wave or storm. /voice → shouldUseRealtimeStream (telephony.ts:1290) checks prerequisites, TTS health, the circuit and the tenant flag, but not the connection cap, so it returns <Connect><Stream>. On the WS `start` frame, registry.acquire returns null (perTenantMax: 50) → `this.closeWs(1013, 'tenant_connection_cap')` (mediastream-adapter.ts:1384). That runs before state.callSid is set, so attemptDegradeToGather cannot run. The stream closes and Twilio ends the call.
findings.impact: Overflow callers hear silence and are disconnected, with no greeting, voicemail or Gather fallback, exactly at peak demand, when lost calls cost the most. The cap is a safety limit, so overflow should degrade rather than drop.
findings.evidence: mediastream-adapter.ts:1379-1385: `if (!lease) { this.logSecurityEvent('tenant_connection_cap_exceeded', …); this.closeWs(1013, 'tenant_connection_cap'); return; }`. `this.state.callSid = callSid` is only assigned at 1391, after this return, and attemptDegradeToGather bails on `!callSid` (1768). connection-registry.ts:27 `perTenantMax: 50`. shouldUseRealtimeStream has no registry check.
findings.fix: In shouldUseRealtimeStream, read `connectionRegistry.count('twilio_media_streams', tenantId)` and return false (Gather) at or above perTenantMax. As a backstop in handleStart, set state.callSid/accountSid before the cap check and call `attemptDegradeToGather('tenant_connection_cap')` before closeWs(1013).
findings.test: Adapter unit test: registry.acquire resolves null and restRedirect is a spy → restRedirect is called with the CallSid and closeReason is 'degraded_to_gather'. Route unit test: a registry whose count is at max → /voice returns Gather TwiML, not <Stream>.

verification.reasoning: handleStart calls registry.acquire (mediastream-adapter.ts:1373-1386), and when it returns null it runs closeWs(1013, 'tenant_connection_cap') and returns. That happens before this.state.callSid and accountSid are assigned (1391-1392). attemptDegradeToGather bails on !callSid (1768), so it could not run here even if it were called. DEFAULT_REGISTRY_CONFIG.perTenantMax = 50 (connection-registry.ts:27), and createConnectionRegistry is called with the default config (app.ts:870). shouldUseRealtimeStream (telephony.ts:1290-1365) checks prerequisites, the TTS credential verdict, the circuit and the tenant flag, but not the registry. The dropped-call sweep runs `compose: createRecoveryComposer({ composerDeps: { gateway: llmGateway, ... } })` (app.ts:6528), which reaches composeBrandVoiceMessage (recovery-composer.ts:66). (2) A tech texts an out-of-office status: sms/tech-status/handler.ts -> createRescheduleProposalsFromTechOut -> draftCustomerRescheduleMessage (customer-message-draft.ts:54). PgAiRunRepository.create binds it to `prompt_version_id`, a `UUID` column (schema.ts:180). Postgres rejects the insert with 'invalid input syntax for type uuid', and the gateway swallows the error: `this.logger?.error('AI-run logging failed (best-effort, LLM call continues)')` (gateway.ts:561-566). The per-tenant usage report, which sums ai_runs.cost_micro_cents (pg-tenant-usage.ts:123), under-counts that spend. The failure-rate monitor reads only ai_runs (pg-failure-monitor.ts:46-60), so a brand-voice outage can never page. findings.evidence: I ran a probe with the real LLMGateway plus composeBrandVoiceMessage and a capturing AiRunRepository (<scratch>). It printed `ai_runs.create promptVersionId = "brand_voice_v1" taskType = brand_voice_v1`. pg-ai-run.ts:71 binds `run.promptVersionId ?? null` into `prompt_version_id`, and schema.ts:180 declares `prompt_version_id UUID,`. findings.fix: Fix it at the gateway seam so no caller can repeat this. In gateway.ts (and the mirror in cache.ts:182), pass `promptVersionId` to createAiRun only when it matches a UUID. Put any other value into the snapshot instead: `inputSnapshot: { messages, temperature, maxTokens, ...(rawPromptRef && !isUuid(rawPromptRef) ? { promptRef: rawPromptRef } : {}) }`. Optionally, migrate ai_runs to add a TEXT `prompt_ref` column and stop overloading the UUID FK slot. Keep composer.ts unchanged, or rename its metadata key to `promptRef`.
findings.test: Add a Docker-gated integration test in packages/api/test/integration/. findings.impact: Each gateway call writes `correlation_id = metadata.correlationId ?? uuidv4()` (gateway.ts:533-534), and almost no call site supplies one, so the value is a fresh random UUID. findings.title: A prompt or model-routing change can reach production without any eval against the real model
findings.trigger: An engineer edits the draft_estimate system prompt, the review public-response prompt (reputation/draft-public-response.ts:112), or a tier model in config/ai-routing.ts, then merges to main. deploy.yml (push to main, line 4) runs only Layer 1 voice-quality plus the offline voice-eval (lines 87-113), and the Railway jobs need only those (line 117). Layer 1 replays cassettes that were recorded from the deterministic in-repo ScriptAwareMockGateway. The required fix for a prompt edit is `npm run voice-quality:refresh`, which re-records from that same mock, so it goes green whatever the real model would do. The offline voice-eval runs a regex rule classifier that the baseline-classifier.ts header says 'is NOT the production classifier'. Nothing on the deploy path calls a real model.
findings.impact: An enterprise customer asking 'how do you know a release didn't make it worse?' gets no merge-time or deploy-time answer for any AI task. Every real-model gate sits off the deploy path. Layer 2 runs only on `push: branches: ["release/*"]` (voice-quality-pre-deploy.yml:29), and production deploys from main; `git branch -r` shows no release/* branch at all. voice-eval-live, whose 200-utterance intent and slot baselines were recorded 2026-09-30, is 'NOT PR-blocking — it runs on a weekly cron' (voice-eval-live.yml:10). Agent Path Smoke is the only real-model PR check. It is path-filtered to packages/api/src/ai/** (agent-path-smoke.yml:19-24), runs 11 classify_intent utterances with a 0.8 pass ratio (line 49, so 2 regressions still pass), and does not run on deploy. It exercises no drafting, brand-voice, review-response, transcription-correction or supervisor prompt. Prompts outside src/ai, such as reputation/*, workers/transcription.ts:353 and config/ai-routing.ts, never trigger it. The only after-the-fact quality signal is the 7-day voice_graded_pass_rate_7d SLO (slo-monitor.ts:254), and it covers voice only.
findings.evidence: pr-checks.yml:160: "Today's entry uses createMockLLMGateway (canned classifier response)". The cassette-refresh runbook: "The runner makes NO live LLM calls and costs $0. `buildCassetteGatewayForScript` wraps `CassetteLLMGateway` around `ScriptAwareMockGateway`... Every recorded entry carries \"provider\": \"mock\"". baseline-classifier.ts:4-6: "deterministic, offline rule-based intent classifier... NOT the production classifier". deploy.yml:117: `needs: [test, voice-quality-gate]`. voice-quality-pre-deploy.yml:29: `branches: ["release/*"]`.
findings.fix: Add a `live-ai-eval` job to deploy.yml (needs: test) and add it to `deploy-railway-dev.needs`. The job should run `run-intent-eval.ts --live --gate --baseline packages/voice-eval/baselines/intent-live.json --max-utterances 200`, the matching slot eval against slot-live.json, and agent:path-smoke --gate; all three are already cost-capped. In agent-path-smoke.yml, widen `paths` to every prompt-defining or routing file (packages/api/src/reputation/**, packages/api/src/workers/transcription.ts, packages/api/src/workers/supervisor-review-worker.ts, packages/api/src/proposals/edit-interpreter.ts, packages/api/src/config/ai-routing.ts), or drop the filter, and make it a required check. Then add a small real-model golden set for draft_estimate (catalog-grounded line items) and brand-voice, so drafting prompts get the same baseline gate.
findings.test: Add a workflow contract test (pattern: packages/api/test/voice-quality/ci-workflow-voice-eval-live.test.ts and ci-workflow-path-smoke.test.ts). It parses deploy.yml and asserts that deploy-railway-dev.needs includes the live eval job, and that the job invokes the live intent and slot evals with `--live --gate --baseline`. It also asserts that agent-path-smoke.yml's paths cover reputation/, workers/transcription.ts and config/ai-routing.ts.

verification.reasoning: Verified. deploy.yml triggers on push to main. Its gates are the `test` job and `voice-quality-gate` (the mock Layer 1 corpus plus the offline intent and slot evals). baseline-classifier.ts:4-6 says outright that it is not the production classifier. pr-checks.yml:160 says Layer 1 uses createMockLLMGateway. voice-quality-pre-deploy.yml runs only on `release/*` or a manual dispatch. voice-eval-live.yml runs on a weekly cron and is 'NOT PR-blocking'; its live baselines are recorded (intent-live.json, 2026-09-30, accuracy 0.94). agent-path-smoke.yml's PR trigger is path-filtered to packages/api/src/ai/** and the smoke scripts, so reputation/**, workers/transcription.ts and config/ai-routing.ts do not trigger it. It runs 11 classify calls at a 0.8 pass ratio. So nothing on the merge-to-deploy path calls a real model, and drafting, brand-voice and review-response prompts have no real-model eval anywhere. The auditor left out mitigations that lower the severity. agent-path-smoke also runs on a DAILY cron (06:30 UTC), mms-vision-smoke runs daily with a real key, and voice-eval-live runs weekly. So a classifier regression shows up within about 24h, though nothing blocks it. One point makes the gap wider: docs/plans/2026-09-08-deployment-tracking.md says Railway's own GitHub auto-deploy is still creating deployments on the same push, and disabling it is 'pending'. If that is still on, any gate added only to deploy.yml can be bypassed. This is an eval-process gap, not an exploitable defect, so medium rather than high.
verification.corrected_fix: Gate at PR merge, not only in deploy.yml. A deploy-time live eval makes every deploy, hotfixes included, depend on OpenAI availability and model nondeterminism. Railway's GitHub auto-deploy may also bypass deploy.yml, so it should be disabled first, as the 2026-09-08 plan already calls for. Concretely: (1) In agent-path-smoke.yml, widen `paths` to every prompt-defining or routing file (packages/api/src/reputation/**, workers/transcription.ts, workers/supervisor-review-worker.ts, proposals/edit-interpreter.ts, config/ai-routing.ts) and make it a required status check under branch protection. Use a skip-pass shim for PRs that don't match the paths, so a required check doesn't hang. (2) Add the cost-capped `run-intent-eval.ts --live --gate --baseline baselines/intent-live.json` and the matching slot eval to that same path-filtered PR job. (3) Add a small real-model golden set for draft_estimate (catalog-grounded) and brand_voice. (4) Optionally add a non-blocking live eval as a post-deploy signal in deploy.yml. Pin all of this with a workflow contract test in the style of ci-workflow-path-smoke.test.ts.

findings.title: AI alerting only pages on platform-wide non-completion; a single tenant's AI outage or a runaway spend loop never pages
findings.trigger: Case (a): one enterprise tenant's call volume exceeds the classifier quota. No production caller sets tenantTier (`grep tenantTier:` finds none outside the resilience layer), so every tenant gets `classifier_standard` (compose-resilience.ts:336-344): maxConcurrency 2 and 1,000 tokens/s refill (tenant-quota.ts:53-58) against a roughly 9k-token classify prompt. Their classify_intent calls throw TenantConcurrencyExceededError or TenantTokenBudgetExceededError (tenant-quota.ts:202-218), which gives 100% failure for that tenant. Case (b): a sweep regresses into re-calling the LLM successfully in a loop, the 26,894-run supervisor_annotate storm shape but completing.
findings.impact: The only AI alert is the failure-rate monitor. Its query is cross-tenant `GROUP BY task_type` (pg-failure-monitor.ts:60), and it alerts on `(total - completed) / total > 0.25` (failure-rate-monitor.ts:155). In case (a), one tenant's total outage is diluted by healthy tenants' traffic and does not breach unless that tenant is more than 25% of platform classify volume. The quota rejection counters are labelled only by tenant_tier (metrics.ts:127-138), so they cannot attribute it either. In case (b), completion stays at 100%, so nothing breaches. gateway_request_cost_micro_cents_total and gateway_request_latency_ms (metrics.ts:57-88) have no consumer: no SLO rule reads them (slo-monitor rules are call_completion_rate, queue_staleness, sweep_lag, voice_turn_latency_p95, voice_graded_pass_rate_7d), and the metrics backend is deferred to '50+ customers' (launch-quality-bar.md:36). A contractual-uptime customer whose AI is down, and a cost spike, are both found by the customer or the invoice.
findings.evidence: pg-failure-monitor.ts SQL: `FROM ai_runs WHERE created_at >= $1 AND created_at < $2 GROUP BY task_type`. failure-rate-monitor.ts:154-155: `const unsuccessful = counts.total - counts.completed; const rate = unsuccessful / counts.total;`. tenant-quota.ts:203-204: `tenantConcurrencyRejectTotal.inc({ tenant_tier: tenantTier ?? 'standard' }); throw new TenantConcurrencyExceededError(tenantId);`. The failure-rate-monitor.ts header records the 23 July incident in which a token-budget exhaustion took classify_intent down without an alert.
findings.fix: Extend PgFailureMonitorRepository and runFailureRateMonitor in place with three rules. (1) A per-tenant rule: `GROUP BY tenant_id, task_type` over the same settled window, with its own volume floor and cooldown key `ai_task_failure_rate:<task>:<tenant>`; idx_ai_runs_tenant_created_at (migration 307) supports this. (2) A spend rule: `SUM(cost_micro_cents)` per window, platform-wide and per tenant, against new config thresholds (FAILURE_MONITOR_SPEND_MAX_MICRO_CENTS and a per-tenant variant). (3) A volume-spike rule per task_type against the trailing baseline. Route all three through the existing alertOperator. Separately, give the capacity issue in case (a), where every tenant gets the same 'standard' classifier bucket, to the resilience workstream.
findings.test: Unit tests for the new pure evaluators: a single-tenant 100% failure inside a healthy platform breaches the per-tenant rule and not the platform rule; spend over the cap breaches with 100% completion. Add a Docker-gated integration test in packages/api/test/integration/ that seeds ai_runs rows for two tenants and asserts the new per-tenant and spend aggregates under withCrossTenantSweep.

verification.reasoning: The core gap is real. PgFailureMonitorRepository.taskRunCounts is a cross-tenant `GROUP BY task_type` over ai_runs. evaluateTaskFailureRate alerts on (total-completed)/total above rateMax with a volume floor. Every slo-monitor rule is cross-tenant as well. Nothing alerts on gateway_request_cost_micro_cents_total or on SUM(ai_runs.cost_micro_cents): the only metric consumer would be the dashboards that launch-quality-bar.md defers to '50+ customers'. So one tenant's partial or total AI outage gets diluted by healthy tenants' traffic, and a loop that completes successfully never pages. Quota rejections do still land in ai_runs as failed rows per tenant, because the quota wrapper sits inside the gateway's provider stack, so the data for a per-tenant rule is already there. Two parts are overstated. (a) No caller sets tenantTier, so every tenant gets classifier_standard: concurrency 2, a 600k-token burst, 1k tokens/s refill. That is rate throttling (a ~66-call burst, then about 6-7 classifies/min sustained at ~9k tokens each, plus concurrency-2 rejections), not '100% failure for that tenant'. (b) The same per-tenant token buckets cap how fast one tenant can spend, cluster-wide when REDIS_URL is set, so a completing runaway loop is bounded per tenant, not unbounded. The unbounded case is a loop that fans out across many tenants. Also, at the current scale of few tenants, one tenant's outage is more likely to move the platform-wide rate. Medium is about right for an enterprise SLA posture.
verification.corrected_fix: Extend the existing monitor in place, as proposed. (1) Add a per-tenant variant of taskRunCounts (`GROUP BY tenant_id, task_type`) with its own volume floor and cooldown key `ai_task_failure_rate:<task>:<tenant>`. idx_ai_runs_tenant_created_at already supports it. (2) Add a spend rule on SUM(cost_micro_cents) per window, platform-wide and for the top-N tenants, with configured thresholds. This should key on the cross-tenant total, because per-tenant spend is already bounded by the quota buckets. A per-task volume spike rule is optional. Route everything through alertOperator. Track separately that no tenant can be given a higher tier (tenantTier is never set), because concurrency 2 for classify is a real capacity limit for a busy enterprise tenant. Tests: unit tests for the new pure evaluators, plus a Docker-gated aggregate test that seeds two tenants.

findings.title: Each supervisor review writes two ai_runs rows, and supervisor_reviews links the one with no tokens, no cost and no served model
findings.trigger: The voice action router reaches the supervisor review gate for a chain head or a ready_for_review action (voice-action-router.ts:2238 and :2642, gate wired at app.ts:7615 with `gateway: llmGateway, aiRunRepo`). runLlmCheck first writes its own ai_runs row (`createAiRun({... model: deps.supervisorModel, createdBy: 'system'})`, reviewer.ts:116-133). findings.impact: One LLM call produces two rows. supervisor_reviews.ai_run_id points at the reviewer's own row (reviewer.ts:159, persisted at :323). That row is completed with only `outputSnapshot` (reviewer.ts:154-157): no token_usage, no cost_micro_cents, and the configured model rather than the model actually served after failover. So 'why did the supervisor hold or annotate this proposal' leads to a row with no usage or cost, and the real gateway row is orphaned with a random correlation_id. Run counts for supervisor_review double in the admin usage report and in the failure monitor's volume floor.
findings.evidence: reviewer.ts:154: `await deps.aiRunRepo.updateStatus(proposal.tenantId, run.id, 'completed', { outputSnapshot: (signals ?? { unparseable: true }) as Record<string, unknown> });`, followed by `return { signals, aiRunId: run.id };`. The gateway response's own `response.aiRunId` is ignored.
findings.fix: Delete the reviewer's manual createAiRun, create and updateStatus, and use the gateway's row: `aiRunId: response.aiRunId ?? null`. Pass `metadata: { proposalId: proposal.id, correlationId: proposal.id }` so the row is findable. This also removes the 'ai_run create failed → deterministic-only' branch, because the gateway already does best-effort logging. Keep the FK guarantee by only linking when response.aiRunId is defined.
findings.test: Unit test in test/ai/supervisor with a real LLMGateway, a stub provider and InMemoryAiRunRepository: exactly one ai_runs row exists after a review, and supervisor_reviews.aiRunId equals that row's id with tokenUsage set. Extend the existing supervisor_reviews integration coverage to assert that the FK resolves to a row with non-null token_usage.

verification.reasoning: Verified in reviewer.ts. runLlmCheck calls createAiRun and startAiRun and persists its own row: taskType supervisor_review, model = deps.supervisorModel, createdBy 'system', a structured input snapshot (lines 116-133). It then calls deps.gateway.complete with `metadata: { proposalId }` (line 139). The gate is wired with `gateway: llmGateway, aiRunRepo` (app.ts:7615-7618), and that gateway was built with the same aiRunRepo, so the gateway writes a second row. Its correlation_id is random, because only correlationId and promptVersionId are read from metadata, so proposalId is dropped. On success the reviewer marks its own row completed with only outputSnapshot (no tokenUsage, no costMicroCents, no served model) and returns `aiRunId: run.id`. supervisor_reviews.ai_run_id (reviews-repo.ts) therefore points at the row without usage data, and response.aiRunId is ignored. The path runs in production: DEFAULT_SUPERVISOR_REVIEW_MODE is 'shadow', which still runs the LLM check, and it is reached from voice-action-router.ts:2238 and :2642. Run counts per review are doubled. Both rows succeed or fail together, so the failure rate is unchanged, but the volume floor and the usage report run counts are inflated. Low severity is right.
verification.corrected_fix: Remove the manual createAiRun/create/updateStatus. Pass `metadata: { proposalId: proposal.id, correlationId: proposal.id }` and link `aiRunId: response.aiRunId ?? null`. One caveat: when gateway.complete throws, the gateway's failed row id is not returned to the caller, so the review row would lose its link on the failure path. Either accept a null ai_run_id there, or, if failed reviews need linking, have the gateway attach aiRunId to the thrown error.
